correctness.rationale: The frozen mathematics and narrowed replacement agree on the slide and mixed-metric counts. From the five XOR generators, translations and generator permutations give exactly the two required minimum-placement orbits: translate a path center to zero; for an independent triple translate one member to zero and use transitivity on intersecting pairs of two-generator index sets. Explicit move legality is one replacement, with XOR in {1,2,4,8,15} for a slide. A separate exhaustive reproduction from the graph and propagation rule (branches/46c08968-162c-4d3f-8745-85ceb2dcef1a/independent_check.py) confirms the 320 minima and all 51,040 unordered distance pairs. It gives 1,120 slide edges, degrees 9 and 5, slide eccentricity six, a single last-layer placement equal to the antineighborhood, and the reported 12,560/27,520/10,800/160 gap counts. Each of the 160 involution pairs is disjoint and has jump distance three. The explicit six-slide and three-jump witnesses are legal. This is exhaustive for the given graph, not an assertion for other folded cubes or the complement. The supplied code was inspected, not executed; the repair leaves its inputs and numerical claims unchanged.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem ties the unique most remote optimum under local sensor movement to a directly defined feature of initial observability: the three initially missed vertices. It quantifies exactly when local moves impose three extra steps and shows a meaningful structural contrast between the two symmetry orbits, despite jump regularity. This is useful independently of the known seed census and is a motivated fixed-graph metric benchmark, not a claim about physical grid movement or a wider family.
